evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from the simulation data about the importance of domain II conformation.

claim: A ligand bound to EGFR acts as a wedge that pushes domains I and III apart, straightening the otherwise bent domain II
source_text: A ligand bound to EGFR (or to another member of the family) acts as a wedge that pushes domains I and III apart, straightening the otherwise bent domain II
evidence_reasoning: This mechanism is cited from Alvarado et al., 2009.

claim: Domain II is bent in the crystal structures of ligand-free EGFR, Her2, Her3, Her4, and dEGFR
source_text: Domain II is bent in the crystal structures of ligand-free EGFR, Her2, Her3, Her4, and dEGFR
evidence_reasoning: This is established structural knowledge from multiple crystal structures.

claim: Simulations showed the transition from the straight to the bent conformation of domain II upon removal of the bound ligand in EGFR and Her3
source_text: We simulated the transition from the straight to the bent conformation of domain II upon removal of the bound ligand in EGFR and Her3 and the consequent development of the gap in the dimer interface
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the MD simulations reported in this manuscript.

claim: For the gap to open, both domain IIs of the two subunits in a dimer need to adopt a bent conformation
source_text: Our simulations suggest that, for the gap to open, both domain IIs of the two subunits in a dimer need to adopt a bent conformation
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference from the simulation data about the structural requirements for gap formation.

claim: The dimer interface of EGFR family receptors is mediated by the receptors and does not involve any direct contribution from the bound ligands
source_text: One feature unique to the dimerization and activation of receptors of the EGFR family (Her2 included), but not to other families of receptor tyrosine kinases (Lemmon and Schlessinger, 2010), is that the dimer interface is mediated by the receptors and does not involve any direct contribution from the bound ligands
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the unique features of EGFR family dimerization.

claim: A bound ligand regulates the conformation of domain II and potentiates it for dimerization
source_text: Instead of directly participating in the dimerization, a bound ligand regulates the conformation of domain II and potentiates it for dimerization
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about the mechanism of ligand action based on structural knowledge.

claim: The structural mechanism for the control of dimerization has been preserved from Drosophila to the human EGFR family
source_text: suggests that the structural mechanism for the control of dimerization has been preserved from Drosophila to the human EGFR family
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the consistent observations across dEGFR and human EGFR family members in simulations and crystal structures.

claim: The sequence identity between the ectodomains of EGFR and Her2 is 40%
source_text: The sequence identity between the ectodomains of EGFR and Her2 is 40%, while that between the ectodomains of EGFR and Her3 is 41%
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative measure of sequence similarity.

claim: The sequence identity between the ectodomains of EGFR and Her3 is 41%
source_text: The sequence identity between the ectodomains of EGFR and Her2 is 40%, while that between the ectodomains of EGFR and Her3 is 41%
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative measure of sequence similarity.

claim: In the region corresponding to EGFR residues 240–309, sequence identity to EGFR is 50% for Her2 and 46% for Her3
source_text: In this region, sequence identity to EGFR is 50% and 46% for Her2 and Her3, respectively
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative measure of sequence similarity in a specific region.

claim: Simulations were performed on the special-purpose supercomputer Anton
source_text: The simulations were performed on the special-purpose supercomputer, Anton
evidence_reasoning: This is a methodological detail about how the simulations were conducted.

claim: The CHARMM22* force field was used for proteins in the simulations
source_text: The simulations were performed on the special-purpose supercomputer, Anton (Shaw et al., 2009), using the CHARMM22* force field (MacKerell et al., 1998; Piana et al., 2011) for proteins
evidence_reasoning: This is a methodological detail about the simulation parameters.

claim: TIP3P was used as the water model in the simulations
source_text: using the CHARMM22* force field (MacKerell et al., 1998; Piana et al., 2011) for proteins and TIP3P (Jorgersen et al., 1983) as the water model
evidence_reasoning: This is a methodological detail about the simulation parameters.

claim: The simulated systems were solvated in water with NaCl at 0.15 M concentration
source_text: The simulated systems were solvated in water with NaCl (Na+ ions were first added to neutralize the net charge of the system, and then equal numbers of Na+ and Cl− were added so that the concentration of Na+ reached 0.15 M)
evidence_reasoning: This is a methodological detail about the simulation setup.

claim: Repeated simulations of a given system produced largely similar results
source_text: Repeated simulations of a given system produced largely similar results
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the reproducibility of the simulation results.

claim: In both simulations of the ligand-free EGFR–Her2 dimer, a gap consistently developed at the dimer interface
source_text: In both simulations of the ligand-free EGFR–Her2 dimer, for example, a gap consistently developed at the dimer interface
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding demonstrating reproducibility across independent simulations.
